items.title: Practice Problems 1, #1–6 (number of significant figures): How many significant figures does each measurement have? (1) 7203 m (2) 1.80 km (3)

body.html: Six measurements; find how many significant figures (sig figs) each has.

Nonzero digits count; zeros between nonzero digits count; final zeros after a decimal point count; zeros that only mark the decimal place do not. In scientific notation, count only the digits in front of the power of ten.

7203 m: 7, 2, 0, 3. The 0 sits between nonzero digits, so it counts. 4 sig figs. 1.80 km: the final 0 is after a decimal point, so it counts. 3 sig figs. 0.00560 m: the leading zeros are placeholders; 5, 6 count, and the final 0 is after the decimal point, so it counts too. 3 sig figs. 30.04 kg: the 0 after the 3 and the 0 after the decimal point are both between nonzero digits. 4 sig figs. 2.7 × 10<sup>8</sup> kg: digits 2 and 7. 2 sig figs. 4.05 × 10<sup>−</sup><sup>14</sup> mL: digits 4, 0, 5 (the 0 is between nonzero digits). 3 sig figs.

check.html: Each count equals the number of digits you would write in the scientific-notation form (for example, 5.60 × 10<sup>−</sup><sup>3</sup> has 3).

body.html: Round each measurement to the stated number of sig figs.

Keep the requested number of digits starting from the first nonzero digit. Look at the next digit: 5 or more rounds up, less than 5 stays. Zeros that are only placeholders stay so the size of the number is unchanged.

2638: keep "26"; the next digit is 3, so round down. Placeholders keep the size: 2600 m, written 2.6 × 10<sup>3</sup> m so the two sig figs are clear. 3.96: keep "3.9"; the next digit is 6, so round the 9 up to 10, which carries: 4.0 km (keep the 0 so there are still 2 sig figs). 0.0087: keep "8"; the next digit is 7, so round up: 0.009 m. 15.396: keep "15.3"; the next digit is 9, so round up: 15.4 kg.

check.html: Each rounded value is within a few percent of the unrounded value, and has the requested count of sig figs.
